direction: D2 Who carries the fashion: communal vs generational change (WP6)

hypotheses.statement: Communal dominance: within-stayer share >= 0.70 (last list position) and >= 0.60 (any role), E = 2022-23 -> L = 2025-26, profile keys.
hypotheses.verdict_note: Prediction met on rho (the pilot-calibrated statistic, deviation D2-1) but not on the literal Kitagawa within share; a purely generational world with the observed co-authorship would also meet it, so communal dominance is not identified by H2a.

hypotheses.statement: Generational increment at first list position: rho_first lower than rho_last by >= 0.2; entrant first-position keys' L NAME share exceeds stayers'.

symmetric_lookback_prior_first_ratio.definition: first-position keys, prior = seen in y-1 or y-2 (symmetric 2-year lookback); E = 2023, L = 2025-26; all papers with a profile first key

hypotheses.verdict: supported on the pre-registered groups; magnitude not robust
hypotheses.verdict_note: The pre-registered contrast holds on the D2 groups, also with two-way SEs; D2 stayers have >= 3 years of presence, so the contrast mixes cohort with tenure: within the same last-position key the entrant-first premium is about half the raw gap, and with a symmetric 2-year lookback prior first keys changed nearly as much as the first-position population.

hypotheses.statement: Not driven by entrant co-authors: (i) on stayers' author-paper rows with key FE, the implied E->L change at share_new_coauthors = 0 is >= 0.5 x the population change; (ii) teams whose keys all appeared earlier (rolling) rise by >= 0.5 x the population rise.
hypotheses.null: change at share_new = 0 <= 0.3 x population change
hypotheses.verdict_note: (i) is contradicted (two-way CI of the ratio excludes 0.5 from below); (ii) is met on the point estimate under the rolling and lag-1 definitions only (CIs reach below 0.5) and fails under the fixed 2021-22 base; not falsified because the CI of (i) excludes 0, although its margin above 0.3x is not significant.

hypotheses.statement: Style vs topic channel: across markers, within-stayer change regressed on population change has slope ~1 (falsified if < 0.7); the generational increment share 1 - within/pop is larger for style than for topic markers.

random_subset_benchmark.note: Under the shared-outcome generational null every marker has dS/d = the null rho, so the slope equals the any-role null rho (ident_results.json -> null_rho_any).

hypotheses.verdict: supported (channel contrast); slope criterion not diagnostic
hypotheses.verdict_note: A random paper subset gives slope ~1.00 and the shared-outcome generational null gives slope = the null rho (~0.78), both above 0.7, so the slope criterion cannot discriminate. The style-topic contrast is informative (the null predicts the same ratio for every marker) and survives equal weighting and dropping both llm_topic and the NAME family.

hypotheses.statement: Pre-LLM replication: with email keys, 2018 -> 2020, the NAME and colon (compound) rise is >= 50% within stayers (any role primary).
hypotheses.null: rho_any <= 0.3 for NAME or for compound (intersection-union)
hypotheses.verdict_note: On the literal pre-registered Kitagawa within share both outcomes fall below 0.3, but that statistic cannot exceed the stayer weight s_bar = 0.22 even under purely communal change. On rho (post hoc for H2e, deviation D2-1) NAME is 1.20 and exceeds the shared-outcome null by a margin whose CI nearly reaches 0; compound is imprecise and the author-weighted compound rho is below 0.5.

S2_1.statement: Even among retitled resubmissions (destination >= 2024), NAME is not added on net.
S2_1.caveat: Pairs are selected on retitling (the export keeps one submission per family); transition rates are not behaviour.
S2_1.verdict: NAME not added on net; lag behind content-fixed drift not established

S2_2.statement: Future-tie placebo: past-collaborator exposure is no larger than future-collaborator exposure in the clean sample.
S2_2.verdict_note: The ordering past <= future holds for NAME, but the llm_topic positive control is not detected in the primary specification and shows the same ordering where it is detected, so the design cannot separate tie contagion from homophily.
